Subject: HorizonTech - Dedicated cluster sizing & ramp options

Hi Anna —

Great talking earlier this week. Per our conversation I attached a concise proposal (HorizonTech_Reserved_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a simple cost model (horizon_cost-model.xlsx). High level: we built three candidate reservation packages so you can match runway to expected usage and procurement constraints. For each we called out: cluster size (GPU count), a guaranteed minimum (min GPUs), and a 6-month ramp plan.

Summary (quick view):
- Option A — Pilot Lane: 12 GPUs (min 8) — 8 weeks onboarding, steady-state at month 3. Good for product-ML experiments and proof-of-concept.
- Option B — Growth Lane: 48 GPUs (min 24) — phased ramp: 25% monthly scale, full by month 4. Best if you expect a meaningful volume increase from Q1.
- Option C — Anchor Lane: 96 GPUs (min 64) — immediate reserved baseline with 20% burst capacity, full warmstart and prewarm credits included. Recommended for mission-critical inference at low latency.

Key operational notes:
- Warmstart credits: we include two weeks of prewarm credits for Anchor/Growth to mitigate cold-cache latency on day one.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to compatible model variants if your primary fleet is saturated; can be limited by region.
- SLA: standard 99.9% uptime; if you need SLA exceptions we included a draft SLA-exception-request.docx (attached).

Please take a look and tell me which option best matches your procurement constraints (budget / minimum commit). Happy to run a modeled burn-rate with the exact traffic profile you shared.

Next steps I propose: 1) You flag preferred option, 2) procurement and legal kickoff (we can pre-fill SOW), 3) schedule technical onboarding window (we recommend 4–6 weeks for pilot to be production-ready).

Attachments: HorizonTech_Reserved_Proposal_v1.pdf, horizon_cost-model.xlsx

Thanks —

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear options and the spreadsheets. A few quick procurement questions before we queue legal: 

1) Minimum commit flexibility — our finance team wants to understand if we can front-load acceptance credits in month 1 to reduce the minimum payable in months 2–3. Any flexibility?
2) Cost variability — is the cost-model shown in the sheet pre- or post-quantization discounts? We plan to use INT8 quantized models for batch jobs but full-precision for low-latency endpoints.
3) On Anchor Lane: what’s the practical lead time to add +20% GPUs once we cross the 70% utilization threshold? We prefer short ramp windows.

Also looping Carlos (infra lead) for the technical timeline. Carlos — if you can confirm whether HorizonTech requires on-site acceptance tests or if a remote canary is fine, that will speed things up.

Appreciate it,

Anna — thanks for the quick questions. Answers below and I expanded the proposal with a short execution playbook (see attached PDF).

1) Minimum commit flexibility
We can offer a smoothing mechanism: front-load up to 40% of the first quarter commit as onboarding credits. Practically that reduces cash outflow in months 2–3 while preserving overall committed usage over the first 90 days. If procurement needs a formal amortization schedule we can attach it to the SOW.

2) Cost & quantization
The cost-model.xlsx shows list pricing for reserved GPUs. We apply model-optimization discounts separately — typically a 10–20% unit-cost reduction when customers enable INT8 quantization for non-latency-sensitive workloads. For mixed workloads (quantized batch + FP32 endpoints) we recommend a two-pool topology: a quantized-heavy pool for batch and a low-latency pool pinned to FP32 instances. We called this out on page 3 of the proposal.

3) Adding +20% capacity on Anchor Lane
With Dedicated, we pre-reserve burst capacity and can enable an automated +20% within 24–48 hours in US regions (shorter if we already have spare capacity in your reserved slab). That action triggers a warmstart flow — KV-cache prewarm and model weights pinned to GPUs. We also include a 2-week warmstart credit to smooth immediate latency.

Execution notes (playbook):
- Week 0: Legal/Procurement sign-off + initial payment schedule
- Week 1–2: Reserved fleet provisioning + access credentials; run a remote canary (recommended)
- Week 3–6: Incremental traffic ramp for Pilot/Growth; ops runbooks handed over
- Month 3–4: Full steady-state for Growth; Anchor is production-ready within the first week after provisioning

If you'd like, I can convert the front-loaded credit offer into a contractable clause for the SOW and send an updated DocuSign envelope.

Attachments: HorizonTech_Reserved_Proposal_v1.pdf (updated), horizon_cost-model.xlsx

Marissa / Grace — forwarding the thread; HorizonTech is leaning toward Growth Lane but procurement pushed on minimum commit flexibility. I proposed front-loading up to 40% of Q1 as onboarding credits (shifts cash timing, preserves ARR).

Negotiation points for us to approve internally:
- Approve 40% front-load credit for HT-2026-042 (applies only to first 90 days) — reduces cash collected in months 2–3 by ~35k but increases chance of committing to Growth Lane (48 GPUs).
- Confirm we can promise +20% burst activation within 48 hours for US regions (ops has to reserve slack). If ops needs a buffer, we should toggle to 72 hours and be explicit in SOW.
- Legal: add an amortization clause so back-end revenue recognition is protected.

If you approve, I'll bake those points into the SOW and prepare the DocuSign packet and the SLA exception draft.
